issues.legal_issue: A defendant may amend a written statement to add an alternative defence where it does not contradict the existing defence or withdraw an admission, and any prejudice to the plaintiff can be addressed by terms.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought the defendant’s eviction on the basis that the defendant was a licensee, while the defendant’s existing written statement claimed that he was a lessee.
The defendant sought to add an alternative plea that, if found to be a licensee, the licence was irrevocable because he had carried out permanent works and incurred expenses in reliance on it.
The proposed alternative plea was connected to the existing dispute and was not inconsistent with or repugnant to the defences already raised.
The application to amend was delayed, but the plaintiff could be compensated by costs.
The plaintiff asserted that licence fees were unpaid, and the court made permission to amend conditional on payment of the arrears and costs.
issues.conclusion: The refusal of the amendment was set aside, and the defendant was permitted to add the alternative defence, subject to payment of the licence-fee arrears and costs.
issues.legal_principle: Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure gives courts a broad discretion to allow amendments in the interests of justice, while requiring judicial care. Under A.K. Gupta & Sons v. Damodar Valley Corporation, an amendment that is only a different or additional approach to the same facts may be allowed even after limitation has expired, but a new claim based on new facts or a new set of ideas prejudicing an accrued right should not be introduced. Smt. Ganga Bai v. Vijay Kumar recognises the breadth of the discretion and the need for care; M/s. Ganesh Trading Company v. Moji Ram holds that amendments should promote justice, that written statements may be amended generously, and that alternative pleas may be taken unless they cause irremediable injustice or withdraw an admission. The proposed defence relied on Section 60(b) of the Indian Easements Act, 1882, concerning when a licence is irrevocable.

rule.if: written_statement_amendment_application and alternative_defence_to_same_dispute and not contradictory_to_existing_defence and prejudice_compensable_by_terms and licence_fee_arrears_asserted

predicates.written_statement_amendment_application: A defendant in a suit applies to amend the written statement.
predicates.alternative_defence_to_same_dispute: The defendant seeks to add an alternative defence addressing the same dispute already raised in the suit.
predicates.not_contradictory_to_existing_defence: The proposed defence does not contradict the defendant’s existing position or withdraw an admission in the plaintiff’s favour.
predicates.prejudice_compensable_by_terms: Any prejudice to the opposing party from allowing the amendment can be addressed by costs or other conditions.
predicates.licence_fee_arrears_asserted: The opposing party asserts that licence fees remain unpaid.
predicates.amendment_permitted_subject_to_payment_o: The amendment is allowed on terms requiring payment of the asserted arrears and costs.

issues.definition: When a defendant seeks to add a non-contradictory alternative defence in the same dispute, and any prejudice can be addressed by terms, the amendment may be permitted subject to payment of asserted arrears and costs.
